translation:
Here begins the Ras of Aharnish ||23||

1. I bow to the One, undivided and indivisible, whose form the Vedas cannot grasp; unaging, deathless, stainless, without form, who created the eighty-four lakh kinds of forms. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

2. Do not spend yourself on anything else, you proud fool. He who brought forth many universes out of His mind, by that very name you cross over existence. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

3. In countless lives you have taken birth; you have borne hardship and much sorrow; and now, in the pride of wealth, you have forgotten Him, and there are yet countless thousands more to come. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

4. Nothing touches Him, nothing clings to Him or defiles Him; in a moment He breaks and fashions ten million universes; He deceives them all, the clever and the simple alike; standing apart, He stages many a play. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

5. He who dwells beyond ten million universes, who but a Vaishnav can grasp Him? His way is one without precedent; remember Him, for through His leela (divine play) Hari gives liberation.

6. Listen, soul, I tell you one secret: do not, in your ignorance, say "I" and "mine". Get yourself across by the name of Parbrahm; in this way your Father will call you home.

7. In the beginning and before the beginning You alone are; all that stands still and all that moves is Your radiance. You are great, and so are Your names; with all the saints, my salutation is to You.

8. There is no likeness for the nectar of Hari's virtues; even knowledge of the spirit is no match for it. Gods and yogis perish at the end of the aeon, but the saints, contented in Hari's virtues, remain unbroken.

9. Many things in the world seem good, but without Hari's virtues they are all a blaze of poison. Where Hari's virtues are loved day and night, there the fear of death has fled.

10. What you see is certainly perishing; why then cling to any of it with longing? Mighty maya has made you blind; the Guru's word is the true collyrium for the eyes.

11. At first the mouth tastes sweetness, and then the fish falls into great agony. Just so the deluded soul is swept along by pleasure; know that death has taken hold, and fate will do its work.

12. The senses are the servants and the mind is the chief minister; driven by them, a man abandons knowledge. Draw your own self away from them, so as to reach the state of Parbrahm and cling there.

13. Gold weighed out, cows and land given away, food and water given with great honour: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

14. They read the Vedas and Puranas to the very end, they performed sacrifices, vows and observances: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

15. They practised austerity and discipline for a long time and gave up the household and the snare of maya: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

16. One accomplishes the yoga of the spirit and gives up comfort and the enjoyment of the finest savours: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

17. They practise truth and purity daily and worship the gods together with meditation: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

18. They serve mother, father and the Guru's feet, and practise forgiveness, compassion and vows: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

19. Vows, pilgrimage, fasting and ritual works, hospitality to guests and strangers, the dharma of compassion to living beings: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

20. They give up slander and abuse of others, though they praise themselves in false disputation: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

21. They cast off desire, anger and envy, and give pain to no one: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

22. They hold back and restrain all the senses; they endure fasting, harsh austerity and cold: yet, having enjoyed heaven, they fell into affliction; without the imperishable state they wandered in misery.

23. The four wombs of birth bring only turmoil and hunger; the earning of dharma brings strong happiness. By the name of Parbrahm hunger is broken; the unmoving state was obtained and every distress removed.

24. Renouncing the world he came to the Guru's shelter, and conquered birth, old age, fear and death. Devotees, follow the Guru's shelter; the savour of the Guru's word holds him every day.

25. Night and day the savour of His qualities has become his very feeling; he has let go of all other moods, good and bad. In the company of the saints joy wells up and overflows. Parbrahm says: how then should any ruin come to him?

26. Dhruv, the sun and the moon abide in the remembrance of Hari; before that they had borne the afflictions of worldly life. Yakshas, kinnars and men became free of poison; Narad set free beings of the three worlds.

27. The sage named Puru and the husband of Rambha: by remembrance they made an end of worldly existence. If your business is to be lord of the earth, then serve king Parbrahm with bhakti (devotion).

28. Consider and look at the body and the universe: no one can set up an equal to Him. Himself without form, He spreads out this whole expanse; He is from the beginning the father of Brahma and Shankar.

29. By the Name Ajamil attained his end; by the Name the courtesan's birth was carried through. Such is the Name and so powerful; why then cling in vain to what brings ruin?

30. Parbrahm, heed this one petition: the deluded soul strays about in the world. Make it pure and take it into Yourself; make it one with You, and grant it happiness.

31. Lord, heed this one petition: this world is Your own utterance. Your own portions repeat Your name; for the whole world, moving and unmoving, this alone is the work.

32. Whoever sings this ras with a single mind, whoever hears this ras with a single mind, is released from the noose of worldly bondage, which is hard to win even for Brahma and Maheshwar. Grant that grace, Lord Parbrahm. Day and night, repeat Hari Parbrahm!

Thus ends Shri Aharnish (the Ras), complete ||23||
